<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains only standard AUR package metadata and function declarations. The top-level code consists of variable definitions (pkgname, pkgver, url, license, depends, makedepends, source, sha256sums) and a source declaration pointing to the official GitHub archive. The `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions are not executed by `makepkg --printsrcinfo` since this command only parses the PKGBUILD file itself for metadata extraction. There are no command substitutions, data exfiltration attempts, or malicious code in the top-level scope. The source URL points to the official project repository, which is expected behavior for AUR packages. Build-related actions (cargo fetch, cargo build, install) are confined to the `build()` and `package()` functions and are not triggered during the printrcinfo operation.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Top-level PKGBUILD has no malicious code; only variable definitions and source declaration.</summary>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard `.gitignore` file for an AUR package. It excludes build artifacts produced by `makepkg` such as the `pkg/` and `src/` directories, package tarballs (`*.pkg.tar.*`, `*.tar.gz`, `*.tar.zst`), and log files (`*.log`). These are entirely conventional patterns for an AUR git repository to prevent accidental commits of build outputs. The file contains no executable code, no network operations, no obfuscated content, and no instructions of any kind — it is purely a configuration file listing filename patterns.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD file represents a well-structured and legitimate package for tensaku, a Wayland screenshot annotation tool. The package follows standard AUR practices with proper SHA256 checksums for verification. The source URL points to the official GitHub repository, and all build functions use standard Rust/Cargo tooling with the `--frozen` flag for reproducible builds. The package() function performs standard installation of binaries, desktop files, icons, shell completions, and license files to appropriate system directories. No suspicious network requests, obfuscated code, or dangerous commands (eval, curl, wget, etc.) are present. The optdepends correctly reference the Wayland compositors hyprland and sway for optional window snapping functionality, which aligns with the package's described purpose. All code appears to serve the legitimate function of building and installing the screenshot annotation application.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard Rust package build with proper checksums, no malicious behavior detected.</summary>
